required_shared_inventory_item_edges.current_scope: For R(a,c)=1+a/c, c>0 (c is this lemma’s denominator, not the speed of light), deterministic errors |δa|≤ε_a and |δc|≤ε_c<c give the exact ratio bound. Write h=(u,v) with ||h||_2=(u^2+v^2)^{1/2}. If the segment from (a,c) to (a+u,c+v) lies in Q=[A_-,A_+]×[c_-,c_+] with A_-≤A_+ and 0<c_-≤c_+, set A_*=max(|A_-|,|A_+|) and K_Q=(A_*+c_+/2)/c_-^3. The exact remainder is (av^2−cuv)/(c^2(c+v)), and its absolute value is at most K_Q||h||_2^2. Quotient limits give the linearization; this quadratic remainder bound proves it is the total derivative, not only a vector of partial derivatives. The proof uses positive denominators and (|u|−|v|)^2≥0 only. No probability, inference, FTC, chain-rule, or compactness premise.
